method.cycle: Q -> BACK -> TRANCEPT -> FORWARD -> COMPARE -> ASCEND_OR_PLATEAU
method.rule: Every spiral must add evidence, add a falsifier/constraint, narrow a blocker, or record plateau. Fit to the working hypothesis is never sufficient.

summary.strongest_historical_model: Crimea 2014: rapid pre-referendum broadcast infrastructure control, source removal, same-frequency Russian source substitution, journalist suppression and high-volume narrative saturation.
summary.strongest_sovereign_foreign_use_bridge: Kazakhstan 2022: public reporting states authorities attempted targeted filtering with Russian DPI before escalating to broad shutdown.
summary.strongest_negative_control: Nicaragua: Russian-linked SORM/surveillance exposure does not automatically imply broad TSPU-like filtering.
summary.hard_claim_ceiling: No public evidence in this run establishes Roskomnadzor/TSPU remote command of sovereign third-country deployments or synchronized multi-country mass activation.
summary.defensible_warning: The capability and partial-precedent chain justifies proactive foreign-vantage and route-aware monitoring; an active global Russian TSPU operation is not established.

passes.result: Pre-2014 pro-Russian/Russian-language influence existed; amplification-not-creation model required.
Chernomorskaya TV/radio removal preceded referendum.
Simferopol broadcast-center control supports infrastructure-first mechanism.
Russian state channels replaced Ukrainian/local channels rather than simple outage.
Major terrestrial transformation largely completed about a week before vote.
Assaults/threats/detention/equipment pressure complemented distribution control.
Control expanded beyond terrestrial broadcast.
Direction of rapid radio transformation supported; exact first-day FM frequency table remains open.
Imported Russian channels plus transformed local media created layered capture.
USAGM comparison shows top news-source set shifted from Ukrainian to Russia-based sources.
Repeated official/state-media delegitimization documented.
High-salience binary threat framing documented, including referendum imagery.
Protection/rescue rationale repeatedly foregrounded.
Contemporaneous denial followed by later admission of Russian servicemen support creates direct contradiction evidence.
Russian democratic-legality framing conflicts with OSCE constitutional assessment and non-observation.
Restoration narrative documented and reflected in public rationales.
Conflict explicitly reframed as Russia-West strategic-security issue.
Kosovo/Iraq/Libya comparisons used to dilute external legal criticism.
Crimea fits RAND high-volume, multichannel, rapid, repetitive propaganda model.
General persuasion literature supports advantage of speed/familiarity; not individual-level proof.
Television had sufficiently high reach for broadcast capture to matter.
Ukrainian channels still had major news audiences; source flip was not merely reflecting total prior Russian dominance.
Audience-side information-source transformation independently measured.
Many users reported no conscious habit change, consistent with content changing underneath familiar distribution channels.
Very high support confirmed by multiple pollsters; propaganda-only causation rejected.
Polling rationales overlap with official fear frames, suggestive but not uniquely causal.
Randomized survey priming significantly shifted conflict-policy support in a Russian sample.
Longstanding pro-Russian currents retained as major alternative causal contributor.
Armed control and suppressed expression prevent pure persuasion interpretation.
Integrated multi-causal model required: force + institutions + distribution + narratives + identity.
Integrated rerouting-to-Russian-censorship proof-of-concept preserved.
Foreign active use bridge closed at local-authority level.
Russian SORM lineage + heavy censorship + aligned narrative environment; remote command open.
Russian-model SORM + active blocking coexist; device-command linkage open.
Russian-origin surveillance procurement + censorship/shutdown history coexist; exact device-event linkage open.
Strong information-control environment; Russian device-to-blocking attribution remains open.
Russian SORM exposure can manifest mainly as surveillance/intimidation without broad mass blocking.
Vendor export does not establish Moscow operational control.
Commercial Russian transit is not an IOC; matched-path fingerprints required.
No demonstrated synchronized common control plane found.
Foreign-vantage measurement required because U.S.-side services may remain healthy.
External-source failure with local/state substitutes healthy is stronger than generic outage evidence.
No timeout/reset alone counts; DNS/TLS/QUIC/SNI/path composite plus replication required.
Effect tied to one path and disappearing on alternate path is a high-value routing bridge.
Vendor commonality raises prior only; synchronized technical behavior must exceed controls.
Time alignment is testable only with pre-event baselines and independent content coding.
Ordinary independent censorship rate/timing must be modeled before labeling coordination.
Management endpoint/vendor remote-access/shared control-plane proof remains the highest-value missing bridge.
FMIC/State strategic package separated from CISA technical and FBI U.S.-nexus evidence.
Capability chain and partial precedents are strong enough for an early-warning research case, not for alleging an active global TSPU operation.
